newsitem.title: INDIA: Egypt, India sign pacts to boost economic ties.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, India sign pacts to boost economic ties.

text.p: Egypt and India signed agreements on Wednesday aimed at strengthening economic ties between the two emerging economies.
The two nations signed agreements on investment protection, civil aviation, diplomatic consultations, tourism, media, and science and technology, the Indian Foreign Ministry said.
Under the civil aviation agreement, India and Egypt can designate one or more airlines to operate services between the two countries on specified routes, the Ministry said.
Egypt, which in 1961 allied with India in launching the Non-Aligned Movement, is the south Asian country's largest African trading partner.

Earlier, Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, who arrived in India at the weekend for a Non-Aligned Movement meeting, said that his nation and India were poised to seize the opportunities thrown up by six years of economic reforms in both countries.
Moussa met Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral earlier on Wednesday.
Indian Foreign Ministry officials said Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak was due to visit India later this year.
India and Egypt also agreed to set up a joint commission to facilitate investment and trade and exchanges in the fields of science, technology and culture, officials said.
Moussa urged Indian businessmen to invest in his country, particularly in a new project establishing a new valley parallel to the Nile, built on two million acres of reclaimed land.
"It will be up for investment in the areas of tourism, road building, airports, and construction," he said.

"We certainly need more investment -- just as you here in India need more investment. We believe that both countries have a lot to achieve together either bilaterally as well as in the context of South-South cooperation," Moussa said.
